positions.claim: NVIDIA's founding 3D graphics algorithm was fundamentally wrong, and the company survived only by admitting it in 1995 and relearning graphics from textbooks.
What makes great companies is a unique, deeply held perspective about the world, not the technology or the market.
NVIDIA's business is accelerating algorithm domains, not building great chips; the chip is downstream of the algorithm.
Deep learning's significance was that it is a universal function approximator and therefore a new way of doing software, implying the whole computing stack gets reinvented.
Founders should reshape the organization to fit themselves rather than adopt conventional management structures; the next CEO can reshape it again.
Founder mode scales — it worked at NVIDIA for 34 years and from zero to trillions in value.
Agents do not need to be 100% accurate to be useful; 80% plus human completion is already valuable.
Fine-grained controllability is the single biggest breakthrough agents still need, ahead of accuracy or raw capability.
Coarse-grained recursive self-improvement already exists in today's agents via markdown files, long-term memory compaction, and knowledge graphs.
Hardware companies must plan 5 to 10 years ahead because a system takes ~3 years to build, ~2 to ramp, and should serve 10 years of use.
Letting employees choose their own AI coding tools rather than standardizing is the better policy during rapid change.
Reasoning from prior knowledge drastically reduces the driving data needed; a couple million miles suffices for a very good self-driving car.
Every company should be able to build its own domain-specific AI, and open source tooling now makes that relatively easy.
AI eliminates tasks but not jobs, and the narrative that AI destroys jobs is exactly backwards.
Software engineering jobs have grown 10% year over year and radiology jobs about 20% in recent years despite automation of their core tasks.
Employment grows because backlogs of ideas, patients, and lawsuits are so large that productivity gains expand demand for labor.
The ChatGPT moment for robotics already happened a couple of years ago, in the imagination-opening sense rather than the productivity sense.
Robotics progress now depends on the same eval infrastructure as agents: real-to-sim environments, grounded physics simulation, and sim-to-real reinforcement learning.
Self-driving cars were the right first robotics market because of market size, standardized technology, and real economic value.
NVIDIA open-sourced its self-driving stack because adjacent autonomy markets like agriculture, mail delivery, and warehouse AMRs are individually too small to justify separate stacks.
Physical AI is already a nearly $10 billion business for NVIDIA and will be its next $100 billion business in less than 10 years.
Modern AI would not exist without open source — Linux, Kubernetes, Torch, Theano, TensorFlow, and PyTorch were prerequisites.
Writing code by hand will be automated away like long division, while hard sciences and systems thinking retain their value.
This is the greatest time in 60 years to start a company because the computer itself has been completely reset.
Resilience and belief in one's ability to learn matter more to founders than knowing the answers up front.
